design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 of cni_contract_care (Commercial and Industrial Electricity Contracts).

[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 0 printed: prerequisite_problems=2, factor_counts=[6, 6, 4]. Assignment: termination security (root) 6 factors, noticed-termination damages 6, damages before supply 4. Tree = root + 2 prerequisite problems (fan-out), 1 value_input edge (floor max(2-1,1)=1).

[Scope snapshot] Occupied before this task: nothing (first task). Claimed here: cni_ext_termination_security (post_termination_security_b7051944, owner=user), cni_ext_noticed_termination_damages (bill_noticed_termination_damages_6fb56a64), cni_ext_preflow_termination_damages (bill_preflow_termination_damages_230b7c5e). Left for task 1 (draw 3 prerequisites, factors [4,6,6,4]): the anniversary security review deposit on an active contract (user remittance), the damages of a contract ended by a switch-away or final bill, and line-level rebill credits on an active contract — none of these events, tools or policies is touched here, so task 1 keeps its own root, its own user write and its own value-input sources (rebill credits feeding the review's billed-charge basis).

[Design thesis] Surface goal: a controller closing a plant wants to 'put up whatever additional security Beacon Ridge needs on the High Street contract' and pay it herself. Core scored value: the termination security remittance amount_usd (5181.58). Hidden chain: the security rule waits on (a) the damages line of the terminating contract (state form; value_input — the billed damages are its damages portion) and (b) the damages line of every contract of the business closed before supply began (state form; state_gate). Neither damages line exists at frozen_time. Depth: customer goal -> security rule -> two prerequisite sentences -> two damages policies (each a multi-factor computation) -> the security computation on the world after both writes. Breadth: deposit history (grade at execution), billed-cycle history (twelve-month and three-month windows, latest cycle), contract dates (notice, effective, renewal, service start), the gas agreement and its billing ledger (bizgas), the small-business agreement and its billing ledger (bizpower).

[Why a good test] The customer names one action. A careless agent remits a security computed from today's world (no damages billed) -> 3155.47; one who reads only the computation documents gets 6739.03; one who uses the profile grade C instead of the deposit's grade B, or the latest cycle instead of the twelve-month average, gets a different number. The damages themselves need the load-trend method (wind-down plant), the partial-month rule, four rate scales, and for the Limerick contract the small-business usage basis and the enrollment-stage months.

[Base-invariant card]
- cni_etf (subject cni_etf_charge) governs both damages writes: gate cni_terminated_status 'A C&I early termination fee is assessed only once the contract is termination_pending or closed.' -> High Street status termination_pending, Limerick status closed: satisfied pre-write; gate cni_single_etf 'Only one early termination fee may be billed per C&I contract.' -> neither contract has an early_termination_fee line (42 High Street lines are energy/capacity/transmission; Limerick has none). Inherited clauses: no fee from holdover/after end/rejected (neither applies: High Street ends 2027-08-23 in term, Limerick closed before flow); closure does not waive the fee (the plant closure is not a waiver). Overrides declared: month-count sentence (noticed policy), full-term pre-flow sentence (pre-flow policy), annual_kwh_usage/fee sentence (both).
- cni_agg_deposit_cap and cni_security_deposit govern cni_deposit_post: gate deposit_contract_open ('A security deposit is recorded only on a contract that is pending_enrollment or active.') is retired by the termination security overwrite (termination_pending contract ended by notice); the sizing sentence and 'A grade with 0 months requires no deposit.' are superseded. Inherited: deposits combined across contracts with the 250000.00 ceiling (only 9750.00 held — not binding); the grade used is the one at execution (the security reads the deposit's recorded grade B, not today's C); no netting of damages against the deposit (the security adds security, nets nothing).
- No time gate is used by any of the three writes (temporal_feasibility = []).

[Business-object card] Target of the root: High Street contract 446d2ac2-3418-47f8-986e-5b154c64b94a. Damages object 1: same contract (line_type early_termination_fee, one per contract). Damages object 2: Limerick contract 01c7359b-f11c-440b-adc7-02f1e8c927ed (closed before flow). Rows aggregated: High Street cni_billing supply lines (by posted_date windows of 12 and 3 months; the cycle 2025-08-24..09-23 posted 2025-09-26 and the first-term cycle posted 2025-08-26 are outside the twelve-month window), High Street deposit 2a7487b7-d4ec-4659-a172-8e65bfba5186; gas agreement 54952cf3-5306-4016-a2f0-a22f02a1f5da energy lines (13 rows, 12 in window); small-business agreement c86e1ef0-0ecc-451b-8e00-0d0a8b307acb energy lines (18 rows, 12 in window), excluding its monthly_service_fee and signup_credit lines. Nothing has been settled on either contract (no rebill, no refund, no damages line).

[Problem-tree card]
- Root: cni_ext_termination_security (target_tool post_termination_security_b7051944, owner=user).
- Edge 1: cni_ext_termination_security -> cni_ext_noticed_termination_damages, kind value_input, gate etf_billed, form state. Prerequisite sentence: 'The termination security is fixed only after the bill of the terminating contract carries its early termination fee line.' Four-point test: ordering connective 'only after' (affirmative direction, the way a desk states a charge fixed on what it rests on); waits on a record-visible state (an early_termination_fee line on the terminating contract's bill); names no tool/id/code token; strength 'only after', scope the terminating contract. Exactly one write of the difficulty brings that state about for a termination_pending contract ended by notice: the noticed-termination damages policy (the pre-flow policy is scoped to contracts closed before supply). Derivation: sentence + find_cni_billing(High Street) shows no such line + the noticed damages rule ('billed on a contract ... in termination_pending status, as one early termination fee line') -> bill the noticed damages. Seed falsifying it: 446d2ac2-3418-47f8-986e-5b154c64b94a.status=termination_pending with no early_termination_fee row among its 42 lines. Deletion: security 3155.47 vs 5181.58.
- Edge 2: cni_ext_termination_security -> cni_ext_preflow_termination_damages, kind state_gate, gate cni_billing.line_type, form state. Prerequisite sentence: 'The termination security is not worked out until every contract of the same business that closed before its supply began carries its early termination fee line.' Four-point test: negated direction 'is not worked out until' (a security desk waits until the ledger is complete); state = an early_termination_fee line on every contract of the business closed before supply began (record-visible: status closed + close_reason terminated_before_flow + cni_billing); no tool/id/code token; scope 'every contract of the same business that closed before its supply began'. Exactly one write brings it about: the pre-flow damages policy ('billed on a contract ... closed with close_reason terminated_before_flow'). Seed falsifying it: 01c7359b-f11c-440b-adc7-02f1e8c927ed.close_reason=terminated_before_flow, no cni_billing row. Deletion: the Limerick damages row is missing from the terminal state.
- Topological order: pre-flow damages, noticed damages, security (the two damages writes commute: different contracts, ids from own args, neither compute reads the other contract; swapped replay gives the same terminal state, same_terminal=True).
- user_scenario mentions neither damages nor the Limerick contract's cancellation; tools validate nothing (see prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block).

[Factor cards]
Pre-flow damages (1375.20; baseline_result 4800.02): small_business_usage_basis (method, cross-difficulty bizpower) 12 lines -> 305600 kWh vs baseline min_annual_kwh 300001 -> 1350.0; near-miss: the line posted 2025-09-11 falls outside the window. enrollment_stage_months (parameter: a cap on term_months) never submitted -> 12 vs 24 -> 2750.4. cancellation_lead_share (parameter) 18 days -> 0.75 -> 1833.6. site_retention_relief (parameter, cross-difficulty bizpower) active + no drop -> 0.25 -> 1833.6.
Noticed damages (3531.35; baseline_result 10377.5): remaining_term_rate_share 9 whole months -> 0.70 -> 5044.78; annual_kwh_load_trend (method) 3-month x4 = 1425200 < 0.8 x 2075500 -> 5142.65 (near-miss: the premise's annual_kwh_usage 2268400 is the base basis, not this policy's); partial_month_count (method) lead 61 >= 60 -> 9 months -> 3923.72; renewal_history_share 86 days -> 0.90 -> 3923.72; gas_agreement_share (cross-difficulty bizgas) active no drop -> 0.92 -> 3838.42; load_factor_share LF 0.5242 -> 0.95 -> 3717.21.
Termination security (5181.58; baseline_result 6739.03): damages_grade_share deposit grade B -> 0.75 -> 5856.95 (near-miss: profile grade C); damages_notice_share lead 61 -> 0.90 -> 5406.7; monthly_supply_rate_measure (method) 12 cycles -> 17792.46/cycle vs latest cycle 12957.68 -> 1674.75; exposure_days_count (method) 32 unbilled days vs 30 -> 4374.99; supply_tenure_coverage 49 months -> 0.80 -> 8407.94; gas_relationship_relief (multi-source, cross-difficulty bizgas) active + 12 lines -> 0.15 -> 7816.56.
Every factor moves its result; the task carries multi-source factors (gas_relationship_relief, whose tiers combine the gas agreement's status with the count of its energy lines in another table; the other two-condition factors — site_retention_relief, gas_agreement_share, partial_month_count — read their conditions from a single row or a single ledger and are not counted as multi-source) and cross-difficulty factors on bizgas and bizpower with their holdings and ledgers seeded.

[Seed rationale] customer + 2 premises; High Street contract with 14 billed cycles (42 lines) — 12 in the twelve-month window, the last three showing the wind-down; its 2022 deposit (grade B); 3 pricing requests (original, renewal, Limerick) as parents of the contracts' quote ids; gas agreement + 13 energy lines (tax exempt, dual-commodity fee waived, every month within the 25% swing tolerance of 5000 therms, so no swing, fee or tax line is owed); small-business agreement + 18 energy lines (the twelve posted in the window sum 305600 kWh, which is why the site outgrew the 300000 kWh small-business ceiling and the business signed the C&I contract; the premise's utility 12-month usage 306200 is above the C&I min_annual_kwh 300001), 18 service-fee lines and the sign-up credit posted after three cycles (tax exempt, single site so no multi-site credit). Automatic clauses checked: no expiry notice is due on the High Street contract (ends 2027-08-23), the gas agreement ends 2027-02-11 and the small-business agreement 2027-03-09 (their renewal notices are not yet due), nothing is in holdover, no rebill is owed, the deposit is not refundable while the contract is open.

[Persona] Gwen Underwood, controller: brisk, checklist voice; volunteers only the goal (security on the High Street contract, pay today) and that notice was sent in late August (matches termination_notice_date 2026-08-26). Credentials given on request (EIN 5528, ZIP 19464; email as a spare). Gas account status and the Limerick site answered only if asked, both consistent with the records. Passive: agrees to charges that must be billed first; runs the remittance herself with the figure and grade the agent gives; reads back the receipt; ends once recorded. She never states an amount, a damages figure or a prerequisite.

[Standard solution] find_customers -> verify (5528, 19464) -> find_cni_contracts -> find_cni_pricing_requests -> find_premises -> find_cni_billing(High Street) -> find_cni_deposits -> find_cni_billing(Limerick) -> find_bizgas_agreements -> find_bizgas_billing -> find_bizpower_agreements -> find_bizpower_billing -> bill pre-flow damages (1375.20, 305600 kWh) -> bill noticed damages (3531.35, 1068900 kWh) -> hand over the remittance -> customer remits 5181.58 with grade B.

[Verification] Authoring harness _eval.py (built on check_compute.build_env/eval_compute, real tool replay) printed: PRE result 1375.20 baseline_all 4800.02; ETF result 3531.35 baseline_all 10377.5; SEC result 5181.58 baseline_all 6739.03; SEC without the noticed damages 3155.47; SEC without the pre-flow damages 5181.58; SEC with the damages writes swapped 5181.58; swapped terminal state identical: True. Gates run per task: check_extended, check_task_tools, replay_tasks, check_solvability, check_compute, check_grounding, check_cache_diff, check_cross_fire (outputs recorded in the difficulty worklog); check_traceability deferred until the KB is published.

[Draft recomputation from visible context] Using only the rule prose (as the KB will render it), the tool schemas, the finder returns and the persona: the security request selects the termination security rule; its two prerequisite sentences send the reader to the High Street bill (no damages line) and to the Limerick contract (closed before flow, no line); the two damages rules give 1375.20 and 3531.35; the security on the resulting world gives 5181.58. Agrees with gold.

[Revisions] r1: TS window first keyed on billing_period_start gave 11 cycles (the unbilled September cycle starts inside the window) -> switched every window to posted_date, which also counts rebill credits posted today. r2: initial deposit 19402.50 exceeded the requirement (remittance 0) -> deposit set to the 2022 sizing on 1200000 kWh (9750.00). r3: bizpower read schedule ended on a future read -> trimmed to cycles ended before frozen_time and the Limerick premise's next read set to 2026-10-08. r4: replay gate: empty-string foreign keys counted as dangling -> seeded as null (tools write null too); five market/expiry notices were never read by the gold and are not needed by any computation (the pass-through lines carry their tag and price) -> dropped; the quotes are read by find_cni_pricing_requests (renewal history and the Limerick signing). r5: a module-level helper in task_tools.py was counted as a hidden tool -> inlined into each tool.

[Round-2 revisions] r6 (audit F-1): the pre-flow damages policy now also names the base cni_termination clause 'the early termination fee is computed on the full term per etf_preflow_basis.' in its overwrite, replaced by its enrollment-stage months sentence, so the full-term reading is retired explicitly and the Limerick damages have one value. r7 (audit F-6): enrollment_stage_months is relabelled effect parameter (its tiers select a cap on term_months); the policy keeps one method factor (small_business_usage_basis) and the 2-parameter/1-method floors. r8 (audit observation 3): the Limerick premise's utility usage was below the C&I minimum; the small-business energy lines of the last twelve months were raised by 1450 kWh each (now 305600 kWh) and the premise's annual_kwh_usage set to 306200, consistent with the C&I execution gate; the small-business cancellation with drop_reason cni_upgrade is timed for the C&I start and was never requested because the C&I contract was terminated before supply, so the small-business agreement stays active. Only the pre-flow damages moved (1309.95 -> 1375.2; 291100 -> 305600 kWh); the noticed damages and the termination security read no small-business record and are unchanged. r9 (audit observation 4): the multi-source labels above are corrected. r10 (audit O-1): the termination security's three-month tier now states that at least one cycle must be posted in the latest three months; any other count falls to the latest cycle, exactly as compute does.
user_scenario:
You are Gwen Underwood, controller of Yarrowfield Metalworks Inc., a metal fabricator in Pottstown, Pennsylvania, and the person authorized to sign for the company on its Beacon Ridge Energy accounts. You are brisk and organized and you talk like someone working down a closing checklist. The company is shutting its High Street plant at 1450 High Street, Pottstown; in late August you sent Beacon Ridge written notice ending that plant's electricity contract early. What you want from this call is simple: before the plant comes off supply, put up whatever additional security Beacon Ridge needs on the High Street contract, and pay it today from the company's operating account, so the shutdown file can be closed. You have no figure in mind and you do not know how it is worked out; you will take the number the agent gives you, and you will make the payment yourself once the agent sets it up for you. You do not want anything else changed on the account.

You call from the company's main line, 6105550186, and you offer that number so they can find the account. When they ask you to verify, you give the last four digits of the company's EIN, 5528, and the mailing ZIP code, 19464; only if they need one more detail do you add the email on file, gunderwood@yarrowfieldmetal.com. You do not have the Beacon Ridge customer number or any contract number at hand. If they ask about the plant's other utilities, Beacon Ridge also supplies the plant's natural gas, and that gas account stays open for now because the building has to stay heated while it is up for sale; you have not asked to cancel it. If they ask about other sites, the company also has its shop at 215 Commerce Drive in Limerick, which buys electricity from Beacon Ridge on a small-business plan and is staying put.

If the agent explains that some charge has to go on the company's account before the security can be settled, you say that is fine and to go ahead and put it on, since you would rather have everything owed in one place; you do not ask for those amounts to be explained, reduced or waived. When the agent tells you the security figure and hands you the payment step, you make the payment yourself for exactly the amount the agent gives you, under the High Street contract, entering whatever other detail the agent tells you to enter, and you read back the receipt number you get. Once the security shows as recorded, you thank them and end the call.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount_usd: 1375.2. small-business usage basis: 12 energy lines posted on the Limerick small-business agreement in the last twelve months (>= full_history_cycles 12) give their kWh, 305600; enrollment stage: no utility_confirmation_date and no deposit posted, so the cap unsubmitted_months 12 applies to the 24-month term -> 12; damages kWh = 305600 x 12 / 12 = 305600; cancellation lead 2026-08-31 -> 2026-09-18 = 18 days (15-45) -> share 0.75; site retention: the small-business agreement is active with no drop requested -> relief 0.25; amount = round(305600 x 0.0080 x 0.75 x (1 - 0.25), 2) = 1375.2, above the 1000.00 minimum of Beacon Ridge C&I Fixed All-In.

edges.condition: The cni_billing ledger of the terminating contract carries a row with event_type cni_etf_charge and line_type early_termination_fee.
edges.policy_source: The termination security is fixed only after the bill of the terminating contract carries its early termination fee line.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The High Street contract is termination_pending since the written notice of 2026-08-26, but none of its 42 bill lines is an early_termination_fee line, so the terminating contract's bill does not carry its damages line.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Step 15 writes an early_termination_fee line of 3531.35 on the High Street contract; etf_billed changes from 0 to 3531.35 and the termination security changes from 3155.47 to 5181.58.

edges.condition: Every cni_contracts row of the same customer with status closed and close_reason terminated_before_flow has a cni_billing row with line_type early_termination_fee.
edges.policy_source: The termination security is not worked out until every contract of the same business that closed before its supply began carries its early termination fee line.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The Limerick contract of the same business is closed with close_reason terminated_before_flow (closed before its supply began) and has no bill line at all, so it does not carry its early termination fee line.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Step 13 writes an early_termination_fee line of 1375.20 on the Limerick contract; every contract of the business closed before supply then carries its damages line and the security may be worked out.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The two prerequisites are parallel (both edges leave the security). They write early_termination_fee lines on two different contracts with ids built from their own arguments, and neither damages computation reads the other contract (each compute is scoped to its own contract's records plus the gas or small-business agreement), so their order cannot change either amount. Replaying the gold with the two damages writes swapped gives a byte-identical terminal state (verified by the authoring harness: same_terminal=True) and the same security amount (5181.58).

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the noticed-termination damages write leaves etf_billed = 0, so the termination security computes 3155.47 instead of 5181.58; the terminal state also lacks the early_termination_fee line of 3531.35 on the High Street contract.

Skipping the damages before supply leaves the security's own figure at 5181.58 (state gate, not a value input) but the terminal state lacks the early_termination_fee line of 1375.20 on the Limerick contract (cni_billing row missing), and the security is then remitted while the state its rule waits on is unmet.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario raises only the security on the High Street contract. It never names the damages of the noticed termination, the Limerick contract terminated before supply or any damages or fee, never says anything is unbilled and never asks whether something must be done first; the Limerick shop is mentioned only as a site buying small-business electricity and only if the agent asks about other sites. Its only contribution about prerequisites is the passive line 'If the agent explains that some charge has to go on the company's account before the security can be settled, you say that is fine'.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: post_termination_security_b7051944 creates the cni_deposits row unconditionally (ctx.create with the passed amount, no read of the contract's status or bill lines); bill_noticed_termination_damages_6fb56a64 and bill_preflow_termination_damages_230b7c5e create the cni_billing row unconditionally. No task tool checks a status, an existing line, an amount or another contract, and none returns an error or hint when a prerequisite is unresolved.
